newsitem.title: UK: UK government to proceed with millennium exhibition.
newsitem.headline: UK government to proceed with millennium exhibition.

text.p: The British government is to proceed with a controversial millennium exhibition at Greenwich in London, an aide to Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Thursday.

Backers became concerned that the exhibition, whose centrepiece is a giant dome, would collapse if the new Labour government, concerned at the cost, withdrew its backing. But the aide said cabinet backed Blair's decision to go ahead.
The exhibition to mark the arrival of the year 2000 was thought up by former deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine who wanted it built by private industry with help from the National Lottery.

But Labour's lukewarm support before the May 1 election which swept it to power meant private companies did not sign up. The estimated budget began to spiral towards one billion pounds ($1.6 billion). But the new government pared that down to 580 million pounds.

Blair told cabinet that, driven on this project by instinct rather than calculation, he felt Britain needed a big project to mark the millennium and boost morale as well as the country's international profile, his aide said.

But the prime minister told the cabinet there would have to be new management, no additional public expenditure, more work on the concept behind the exhibition and a clear and lasting benefit for the whole country. ($ = 0.609 British Pounds)
